shower.thought: We spend the first part of our lives learning how to be ourselves, and the second part unlearning it.
The worst timeline might be the one where everything works out exactly as planned.
You've probably had the same conversation with different people and never realized you were the inconsistent one.
Memory isn't about what happened—it's about the last time you remembered what happened.
The people who say they never think about dying probably think about it the most.
You can't miss something you never knew existed, which is why ignorance about certain things might actually be a gift.
Every time you learn how something works, you lose the ability to be amazed by it.
Your embarrassing moment from seven years ago only exists because you keep resurrecting it.
The scariest words aren't "I don't love you anymore"—they're "I don't think about you at all."
You've been shaped more by conversations that felt casual than by ones that felt important.
We call it procrastination, but sometimes you're actually waiting for yourself to become a different person who can handle it.
The things you're most defensive about are usually the things you're not quite sure about yourself.
You're never really late—you were just early to the next thing.
Most of your opinions aren't actually yours; they're just the most recent convincing argument you heard.
We preserve our youth by refusing to update our self-image, then wonder why we feel stuck.
The reason you can't remember what you ate last Tuesday is because it didn't matter, and your brain was right not to waste space on it.
Every friendship ends exactly once, and most people never see it coming.
You probably wouldn't like the person you were five years ago, which means you wouldn't like the person you'll be in five years either.
The moment you understand someone completely is usually the moment the relationship starts to change.
You're nostalgic for versions of people who don't exist anymore, not the actual people themselves.

motivational.thought: The man who moves a mountain begins by carrying away small stones. — Confucius
Comparison is the thief of joy, but progress is its antidote. — Unknown
You are not behind. You are not lost. You are exactly where you need to be to become who you're meant to be. — Unknown
The only way out is through. — Robert Frost
Success is not final, failure is not fatal: it is the courage to continue that counts. — Winston Churchill
Your limitations live only in your mind. What you believe, you can achieve. — Unknown
Small progress is still progress. A life changed by tiny choices is a life transformed. — Unknown
The obstacle is not blocking your path—it is the path. — Ancient Proverb
Regret for the things we did will fade away over time, but regret for the things we didn't do is the one that stays forever. — Unknown
Do not wait for perfect conditions. They will never come. The time is always now. — Unknown
You can't heal what you won't acknowledge. You can't grow in what you won't face. — Unknown
Every expert was once a beginner who refused to quit. — Unknown
The person you will become is built on the decisions you make today. — Unknown
Courage is not the absence of fear. It's moving forward anyway. — Franklin D. Roosevelt
Your past does not determine your future—your next choice does. — Unknown
Discipline is just choosing what you want most over what you want now. — Unknown
The only permission you need is the permission you give yourself. — Unknown
What we fear doing most is usually what we most need to do. — Tim Ferriss
The best time to plant a tree was 20 years ago. The second best time is today. — Chinese Proverb
Your value is not determined by your productivity. But your freedom is. — Unknown

darkjoke.thought: I told my friend he was adopted. He said, "I know." I said, "No, I mean just now, by the state."
My therapist asked why I was so defensive. I said, "Who told you that?" Turns out it was my last three therapists.
I went to a suicide prevention seminar. The motivational speaker really hung in there for most of it.
My dad said, "Son, I'm not mad, I'm just disappointed." I said, "Why not both?"
I tried to make a belt out of herbs once. It was a waist of thyme. My therapist said that joke was a cry for help.
My friend said nobody likes him. I said, "That's not true." He said, "Name one person." I said, "Okay, that's fair."
I told my son he was adopted. He cried and said, "Why didn't you tell me sooner?" I said, "We were going to, but you kept being so helpful around the house."
My wife said I never listen to her. At least, that's what I think she said; I wasn't really paying attention.
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left us. On the bright side, he seems really happy with his new family.
I asked my therapist if I was crazy. She said, "Not crazy, just statistically above average for self-sabotage."
My coworker asked why I looked so tired. I said, "I've been having trouble sleeping." He said, "Have you tried not thinking about work?" I've been thinking about that for three days now.
I went to a motivational speaker who said, "You can do anything you put your mind to!" I said, "Okay," and left. Haven't shown up to work in weeks. Turns out he was right.
My date asked if I had a five-year plan. I said, "Yeah, but the statute of limitations varies by state."
I told my mom I wanted to be a comedian. She said, "Honey, you're already hilarious." I said, "Thanks." She said, "I wasn't complimenting you."
My doctor said I needed to lose weight. I said, "Good news—I've been working on it my whole life."
My friend said he was having an existential crisis. I said, "At least you exist." He didn't laugh. He's still not talking to me.
I asked my boss for a raise. He said, "Do you know what we call people who do your job for less money?" I said, "What?" He said, "Literally everyone."
My girlfriend asked if I still loved her. I said, "Of course." She said, "Then why do you sigh every time you see me?" I said, "Allergies."
I told my friend I was going through a rough patch. He said, "It'll get better." It's been five years. Either he was wrong or I've adapted to the pain, which is somehow worse.
My therapist asked what my biggest fear was. I said, "Disappointing people." She said, "Well, you're doing great."
